speaker: Doctor
text: That will help narrow things down. To get started, can you describe exactly what the swelling feels like—is it hard and fixed, or soft and fluctuant? Also, have you noticed any changes in color or temperature of the finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, that sounds like a significant forceful injury. Given the mechanism of injury, do you notice any deformity, or is the finger straight but swollen? Also, have you experienced any difficulty moving the finger or any numbness in the tip?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Bunion of the Extensor Tendon)

The previous diagnosis of Pyelonephritis is incorrect; that is a kidney infection and does not match your finger injury. Based on your inability to flex the distal joint and the extended resting position, you have likely sustained an avulsion injury to the extensor tendon. Do you have any numbness or tingling in your fingertip?

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
